item.description:
• Choose your languages. A new Languages menu in the panel. With one language every call is transcribed in it; with several, each side gets whichever of them it sounds like — judged on the stretches with the most talking, not the first 30 seconds, which had turned a German call into Icelandic and Spanish.
  • Your side survives a headset switch. When AirPods or a headset disconnected mid-call, the rest of your side was recorded as silence. Recording now carries on with the Mac microphone.
  • Fewer lost lines from the other side. What they said while you were talking was sometimes dropped as echo; it is now dropped only when it repeats your words. The “Vielen Dank.” whisper used to put over silence is gone.

• Recordings get names. On macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence, each recording is titled on your Mac, e.g. “2026-11-23 13.22.17 – Reform – Challenge-App”, with a short summary and to-dos in meta.json. Elsewhere recordings keep their date names, as before.
  • ~30× less disk space. Once transcribed, the audio is stored as AAC (.m4a) — about 40 MB per hour instead of 1.2 GB. Earlier recordings are compressed the first time this version starts.
  • Your side of browser calls is back. During calls in Safari (and other apps using voice processing) your microphone was recorded far too quietly and left out of the transcript. It is now picked up.

• Calls on a Bluetooth headset no longer record the other side at double speed.
  • If a recorder stops mid-call, the transcript is still made from what was recorded.

• Offers to record when a call starts, and to stop when it ends.
  • Recordings survive sleep, audio device changes and quitting.
  • Crash fixes in the microphone recorder.
  • Updates now arrive in the app.
